_comment: Committed retrieval baseline. /eval compares against this. Update it deliberately, in the same PR as the change that moved it, with the reason in the commit message.
note: First baseline on the frozen 42-question set (10 original + 32 hand-verified, chunk-first; 50 gold chunks over 37 of the 48 papers). Supersedes the 10-question directional baseline. MRR is truncated at max(k_values), so it is MRR@10 here and rises to 0.584 when k=100 is scored - always quote it with its depth. Headline finding: recall@1 0.393 vs recall@20 0.869 means most gold material IS retrieved but ranked badly, so reranking is the main lever; but recall@100 0.940 leaves ~6% of gold chunks unreachable at any practical depth, which is a genuine coverage gap and revives the case for hybrid retrieval. The reranking-vs-coverage argument that follows from these numbers is recorded in docs/decisions/008.
